source_reviews.independent_solution: Parallel distinct planes have parallel normals. A slant line to alpha intersects it, so its direction v has nonzero normal component, and v is not parallel to the normal. The same two properties hold for beta. Equivalently the line intersects beta and cannot be perpendicular to beta, because theorem 19 with alpha and beta exchanged would then make it perpendicular to alpha. Therefore it is also a slant line to beta.

Its opposite sides AB and CD are equal. If A=C, B=D and equality is immediate.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Let E be the midpoint of CD. AC=AD and BC=BD imply A and B both lie in the perpendicular-bisector plane Pi of CD, so Pi contains the noncollinear points A,B,E and is perpendicular to CD. Reflection in Pi fixes A,B and exchanges C,D. Let P,Q be midpoints of AC,BC, and let R lie on CD with CR=CD/4. Homothety with center C and ratio 1/2 sends A,B,E to P,Q,R; hence PQR is in the plane perpendicular to CD through the prescribed midpoint Q of BC. This plane cuts exactly edges CA,CB,CD and the section is triangle PQR. Let U,V be midpoints of AD,BD and let S on DC satisfy DS=CD/4. The corresponding upper plane through U cuts exactly DA,DB,DC and gives triangle UVS. Reflection in Pi maps P to U, Q to V, R to S, proving congruence. Alternatively PQ=UV=AB/2, PR=US=AE/2, QR=VS=BE/2 proves SSS. The two sections are parallel, lie on opposite sides of Pi, and do not pass through E.
